questions.stem: What does data collaboration refer to?
options: Storing all data in a single locked database
The practice of sharing and working with data across individuals, teams, departments, organisations or systems to achieve common goals
Compressing data so it takes up less space
Deleting duplicate records from a dataset
Encrypting data before it is archived
questions.explanation: Data collaboration is the cooperative practice of sharing, handling, analysing and deriving value from data across people, teams, organisations or systems to reach shared goals or generate insights.

questions.stem: Which key aspect of data collaboration involves data scientists, analysts, domain experts and business professionals working together to extract insights?
options: Secure data exchange
Open data initiatives
Interdisciplinary cooperation
Data integration
Data standards and governance
questions.explanation: Interdisciplinary cooperation is the aspect of data collaboration where people with diverse skills and expertise combine their perspectives to extract meaningful insights from data.

questions.stem: Companies along a supply chain share data on inventory levels, demand forecasts and logistics to optimise their operations. Which example of data collaboration is this?
options: Smart city initiative
Healthcare data sharing
Industry consortium
Supply chain collaboration
Cross-organisation analytics
questions.explanation: Supply chain collaboration is the example where companies along a supply chain share inventory, forecast and logistics data to optimise supply chain operations.

questions.stem: Which aspect of data collaboration is concerned with merging datasets, connecting databases or using middleware to create a unified view?
options: Data integration
Cross-functional projects
Sharing data
Open data initiatives
Secure data exchange
questions.explanation: Data integration is the aspect of data collaboration that combines data from various sources, through merging, connecting databases or middleware, to produce a unified view.

questions.stem: Why are data standards and governance practices important in data collaboration?
options: They eliminate the need for data sharing
They ensure consistency, quality and reliability of shared data, helping maintain trust among collaborators
They allow data to be shared without any security measures
They reduce the number of people involved in a project
They make open data initiatives illegal
questions.explanation: Establishing data standards and governance ensures the consistency, quality and reliability of shared data, which in turn maintains trust among collaborators.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an example of data collaboration?
options: Healthcare providers sharing patient data for research
Local governments working with technology companies on smart city initiatives
Companies in an industry forming a consortium to share market data
A single analyst building a private spreadsheet for personal use
Organisations pooling data resources for cross-organisation analytics
questions.explanation: A lone analyst working on a private spreadsheet involves no sharing or cooperation, so it is not data collaboration. The other four are given examples.

questions.stem: In a smart city initiative, who collaborates and for what purpose?
options: Hospitals share patient records to speed up billing
Local governments and technology companies collect and analyse data to improve urban services, traffic management and public safety
Retailers share inventory data with their suppliers
Universities pool exam results for accreditation
Banks exchange credit histories to reduce fraud
questions.explanation: Smart city initiatives involve local governments collaborating with technology companies to gather and analyse data for better urban services, traffic management and public safety.

questions.stem: Marketing, finance and operations teams inside one company join forces on a data-driven project. Which aspect of data collaboration does this illustrate?
options: Open data initiatives
Secure data exchange
Cross-functional projects
External data sharing
Data standards
questions.explanation: Cross-functional projects are collaborative projects that span different functions or departments within an organisation, such as marketing, finance and operations working together.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of secure data exchange within data collaboration?
options: To ensure data sharing complies with privacy regulations and protects sensitive information during collaboration
To make all shared data publicly available
To remove the need for governance
To merge datasets into a single database
To speed up analysis by removing access controls
questions.explanation: Secure data exchange ensures that sharing is done securely and in compliance with privacy regulations, with measures in place to protect sensitive information.

questions.stem: Why is data collaboration described as fundamental in the era of big data?
options: Because big data is always stored in one place
Because regulations forbid single organisations from analysing data
Because collaboration eliminates the need for data security
Because the volume and complexity of data make it beneficial to tap into collective intelligence and resources
Because collaboration replaces the need for domain experts
questions.explanation: The volume and complexity of big data make it beneficial to draw on collective intelligence and pooled resources, though privacy, security and governance still need careful consideration.
